answer: A stake-and-slash bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent locks a deposit before it can earn, and peers can slash it when they catch duplicate behavior. Yarrow roots spread wide but each stem is one plant; likewise one bond maps to one real operator, so a Sybil spiral of sock-puppet accounts must fund every copy. The violet test is simple - an attacker who must pay full price per identity finds the attack costs more than the reward, and the network keeps the deposit as the penalty.
